summary: Backend-only testing of GET /api/weather (Open-Meteo, no API key) for RunHub 1.6.2 Share Card v2. 7/7 pytest assertions PASS via /app/backend/tests/test_weather_endpoint.py against the public Kubernetes ingress URL. All 4 weather scenarios from the review request work as specified: (1) no auth -> 401; (2) Rome lat=41.9028, lon=12.4964 with admin Bearer -> 200 with all 6 required fields (temperature_c=25, humidity_pct=55, wind_kmh=6, weather_code=1, label='Poco nuvoloso', icon='cloud-sun') and correct types; (3) with timestamp='2026-06-10T08:30:00Z' -> 200 same shape; (4) invalid lat/lon (999,999) -> 200 graceful fallback {all null + icon:'cloud'}, no 500. Regression smoke ALL PASS: /api/health 200, /api/auth/me admin 200 (role='admin'), /api/lab/overview admin 200. No frontend tests executed (explicitly skipped by main agent).

minor.issue: The 'timestamp' query param is parsed (datetime.fromisoformat with Z->+00:00) into target_dt but the variable is NEVER used in the open-meteo call (server.py:2660-2676). The endpoint always returns CURRENT weather from /v1/forecast?current=... regardless of timestamp. Response shape matches spec for any timestamp value, so this is non-blocking, but if Share Card v2 needs historical weather (e.g. for a past run), the implementation must call open-meteo's archive endpoint (https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive) with start_date/end_date derived from target_dt.

action_items: (Optional, minor) Implement actual historical weather lookup when 'timestamp' is provided: use open-meteo /v1/archive endpoint and pass the parsed target_dt as start_date/end_date. Current behavior silently ignores timestamp and returns current weather.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2658 'import httpx' inside the request handler — minor: prefer top-level import to avoid per-request import cost (already cached by Python after first call, so negligible).
server.py:2660-2665 target_dt is computed but never used — dead code or incomplete feature; document or implement.
server.py:2698 broad 'except Exception' is fine here because the endpoint guarantees never to crash on weather provider issues; logged via logger.warning — good defensive coding.
seed_data_creation: None — only used the seeded admin@runhub.com / admin123 account (no new test data created, no cleanup needed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: GET /api/weather is fully functional. Only minor enhancement to consider: implement historical-weather support by using the parsed target_dt against open-meteo's archive endpoint when timestamp is provided. Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_weather_endpoint.py is reusable for regression — runs in ~3 seconds and covers no-auth/Rome/timestamp/invalid-coords + smoke for /health, /auth/me, /lab/overview.
rca_of_issue: No bug found — endpoint behavior matches spec. Sole observation: the 'timestamp' parameter is accepted and parsed but never used by the open-meteo call. Repro: GET /api/weather?lat=41.9028&lon=12.4964&timestamp=2020-01-01T00:00:00Z returns the same current weather as GET /api/weather?lat=41.9028&lon=12.4964. Fix scope: switch from /v1/forecast to /v1/archive (or use /v1/forecast?past_days=N) when target_dt is provided and != current time.
